Club life is a decent slice of life romance story with some comedy and slight background music.
The story itself is good and we have many different choices to select, which makes it hard to find a route without, let's say, cheating our way, thanks to guides. I did like the different stories, but what I did dislike was that each story is all overlapping in text too much, to the point that half of a storyline for a character gets repetitive and has to be reread more than once, which I mostly ended up skipping.

Art style and character sprites are acceptable, it isn't the big arts, but I still find that it could have been a bit more detailed and precise.

Overall, I can recommend it further, but the repetitive texts for each story and defo a loss of points.

Dharker Studio does it again.

Club Life is a short slice of school life VN with multiple endings. It is also one of earlier Dharker's VNs.

Story's main theme is about school clubs and slow romance options. There are three girls/clubs but only two can be chosen each time, so it feels a little bit like a forced replayability if you want to see/complete all as all girls have different interactions with each other. Reaching all 6 endings require some effort since there are a lot of choices, and not all are obvious. Story itself is neither good nor terrible; It generally fluctuates about average. Some sub-stories could be better explained and characters lack proper development but overall writing is ok.

Art of this game is rather weak. Character sprites were heavily inspired by the Japanese drawing style but still feel western. Lack of details, especially in h-scenes is glaring. If your motivation is the ecchi part then don't bother, you'll be very disappointed. Also, even though it's a short VN, the number of CGs is low. Backgrounds are decent at least. 

Music eh... I liked it way more than expected from such a budget title. I liked it enough to add to my playlist for some reason. It is a very subjective opinion but I won't lie here. In my books most tracks were above average, and I enjoyed listening to them. 

No bugs encountered.

Overall, a short slice of life VN with an average story, multiple endings, ok art and surprisingly good music. I enjoyed this title more than expected but it is only barely above average when compared to similar VNs. Still, can recommend: 6.3/10

I was surprised by how much I enjoyed this title.  With three main girls, plus the teacher, you can definitely do 2 main play-throughs of about 3 hours each before you feel like fast-forwarding some of the content because of repetition.  I think there are six "final" endings.  So a couple more play-throughs with saves at key decision points (easily 20+ per game), should complete all the girls' storylines and clear the achievements.  The well-implemented fast-forwarding mechanics allow easy skipping of common-element parts that might repeat.

The game looks to be originally designed in English so there are no spelling, grammar, or translation issues.  The storylines are all fun and intriguing with unique mystery and romance plots for each girl and a lot of unique scenes/background art.  The user interface is terrific and the artwork is all high quality.  The gallery has 18 images spaces, some of which you can click on and drill down 5 or 6 deep to replay the game's H-scenes, which are very tasteful and HQ. 

Definitely a great game and I will be getting a rank 5 badge to support this top quality content!  IMO, Club Life is a perfect "Intro to VN" title if someone is looking for recommendations or to gift!

This is a fun little visual novel. It stars Sean as a senior trying to get through the year and into college. Unfortunately, his advisor wants him to broaden his horizons, and makes him join two clubs in order to gain a recommendation. Depending on which path you choose, you can meet three girls. Melissa and Janet are in the athletic clubs, while Kylie is in the newspaper club. Depending on how serious you are in those clubs, you can end up being able to ask one of the girls to prom. And if you have done the right thing, they might even accept and begin a relationship with you. There is also a chance that the teacher advising you, Ms. Raven might... be interested in you, too.

There is an explicit patch, but most content is at the end of the paths (there is one CG on one path that might also be affected). I'm not really sure it adds anything to the story (though being a visual novel, and the most explicit content is after the final choice... I guess it is a guarantee that you will live happily ever after with your chosen girl).
